  "text": "The path to the boathouse sloped between black rocks slick with spray. Behind them, the bell kept ringing—slow, patient notes that seemed to follow their footsteps.

Ada reached the door first. The brass key turned with a stubborn scrape, and the hinges groaned as she pulled it open. Inside, nets hung from the rafters like sleeping things. Peter found the skiff beneath a heap of rope and shoved the netting aside.

“Help me,” he said.

Mara grabbed the bow. Together they dragged the boat toward the water. Ada fumbled for the oars, then stopped. Her face had gone pale.

Across the cove, Elian stood at the shore. The weed-crowned figure loomed behind her, one long arm resting on her shoulder.

The bell fell silent.

“Get in,” Mara said.

Peter looked down at the compass. Its needle spun wildly, then settled—not east, but toward Elian.

“She told us to take the channel,” Ada whispered.

“She told us not to look back,” Peter said.

The figure leaned close to Elian’s ear. Even across the water, he heard his mother’s voice, soft as a lullaby.

“Peter, darling.”

The skiff rocked against the stones. He could row away. He could obey the last thing Elian had asked of them. But the compass needle trembled, pointing straight at the shore, and the hook beneath his ribs pulled tight.

Mara took his hand. “Whatever you choose, choose quickly.”

Peter stepped out of the skiff.

The water closed over his boots, black and freezing. Behind him, Ada called his name. Ahead, Elian lifted her eyes and shook her head once.

Then Peter heard the bell ring from beneath the sea."
